source_user: A service receives a mix of short prompts and long generations. Design an evaluation plan that reports TTFT, TPOT, throughput, queueing, and P99 latency. Scenario variant 23: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: separate prefill and decode behavior; fix workload distribution; report warmup; use repeated trials; capture GPU memory and request-level traces.
corrected_answer: Assume a fixed model and tokenizer, serving/runtime build, hardware, precision, scheduler and batching policy, sampling settings, request prompt/output-length distribution, load points, correctness checks, and P99 SLO. Treat the result as applying only to these conditions. Hypothesis: at each prespecified load, configuration B changes paired TTFT, TPOT, queueing, throughput, and P99 latency relative to A in warm steady state while preserving correctness and the P99 target; reject that claim if the prespecified confidence interval or threshold rule is not met. Run repeated randomized paired A/B replays of identical requests on isolated hosts, randomizing order and excluding warm-up. Instrument queue admission, dispatch, prefill start/end, first-token time, every decode-token timestamp, completion, cancellation, error, retry, and admission failure. Report TTFT, TPOT, end-to-end and queueing delay, request/token throughput, P50/P95/P99/P99.9, uncertainty, and saturation, stratified by prompt length, output length, and load. Capture GPU/CPU memory and utilization, batch sizes, cache/paging, OOMs, evictions, power/thermal state, and request traces; log versions, kernels, network and background load, and workload drift. Confounders include thermal throttling, host contention, cache warmness, dynamic batching, retries, and load imbalance. Roll back on correctness or error-rate regression, OOM/admission instability, or a prespecified P99 breach. Require independent replay and do not generalize beyond measured workload, hardware, and configuration boundaries.
risks: Tail metrics and throughput depend on workload mix, arrival process, scheduler, and batching; uncontrolled changes can invalidate the comparison.
Prefill/decode contention, retries, cache or paging behavior, thermal throttling, and host interference can shift TTFT, TPOT, and P99 differently.
evidence_required: Record exact deployment, workload distribution, load points, warm-up exclusion, repetitions, event timestamps, correctness checks, and resource telemetry.
Use paired uncertainty intervals and prespecified SLO/rollback thresholds, then verify the finding on an independent replay.
